title: Pullback of the hyperplane module under the Segre embedding
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $m,n\geq0$, and $P=\mathbf P^m_S\times_S\mathbf P^n_S$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. Let $\sigma:P\to\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_S$ be the Segre morphism [def-chow-segre]. Write $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r_S}(1)$ for the invertible module whose restriction over each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ is the degree-one twisting module on $\operatorname{Proj}(A[T_0,\ldots,T_r])$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-sc-invertible-module]. Then there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_P$-modules $$\sigma^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_S}(1)\cong p_1^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^m_S}(1)\otimes_{\mathcal O_P}p_2^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_S}(1),$$ where pullback and tensor product are [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The assertion includes empty $S$ and $m=0$ or $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding, proof: the displayed invertible sheaf pr_1^*O(1) tensor pr_2^*O(1) and its product generating sections; the pullback identification in lemma-projective-space (the projective-space representability lemma).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-symmetric-proj-tautological-chart-gluing] to the free modules of ranks $m+1$ and $n+1$. Their tautological quotient sections are the standard coordinates $X_i$ and $Y_j$ of the affine-local degree-one twists in this statement. Apply the quotient-pair bijection of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] to the $S$-morphisms $p_1,p_2$: their pulled quotient maps are surjective, so the sections $x_i=p_1^*X_i$ and $y_j=p_2^*Y_j$ generate $A=p_1^*\mathcal O(1)$ and $B=p_2^*\mathcal O(1)$. These are invertible, and $L=A\otimes B$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1).

source.place: Tags 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding), first construction paragraph; 01OA (section-projective-bundle), quotient-functor discussion; 01OE (lemma-projective-space-bundle).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-tensor-generating-sections] for two factors, the $(m+1)(n+1)$ sections $s_{ij}=x_i\otimes y_j$ generate $L$. Thus [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] gives a surjection $q:h^*\mathcal O_S^{\oplus((m+1)(n+1))}\twoheadrightarrow L$, sending the $(i,j)$-th basis section to $s_{ij}$, where $h:P\to S$ is the structure map. Here the source is the free module on these basis sections, using $h^*\mathcal O_S\cong\mathcal O_P$.

source.place: Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding), product generating sections; modules.tex Tag 01AO (lemma-tensor-product-globally-generated).

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] on this $q$ to obtain $F:P\to\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_S$. The morphism $\sigma$ of [def-chow-segre] is defined on the base-change projective spaces $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)$; transport it to the relative-Proj spaces of the statement through the canonical isomorphisms $\theta$ of [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] for $r=m,n,(m+1)(n+1)-1$. Over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ each $\theta$ is the Proj comparison fixing every coordinate, so on $D_+(X_i)\times_U D_+(Y_j)$ the transported $\sigma$ maps into $D_+(Z_{ij})$ by $Z_{kl}/Z_{ij}\mapsto(X_k/X_i)(Y_l/Y_j)$, the multihomogeneous coordinates of [def-chow-segre]. Cover $P$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ over such $U$ on which $A,B$ have frames $e,f$; write $x_k=a_ke$, $y_l=c_lf$ and take $l=e\otimes f$, so $s_{ij}=b_{ij}l$ with $b_{ij}=a_ic_j$. By the frames and transitions $X_k=(X_k/X_i)X_i$ of [lem-trf-symmetric-proj-tautological-chart-gluing], $D(a_i)=W\cap p_1^{-1}D_+(X_i)$ and $X_k/X_i$ pulls back to $a_k/a_i$ there; likewise for $c$. Hence $D(b_{ij})=D(a_i)\cap D(c_j)$ and on it $\sigma$ is the $U$-morphism into $D_+(Z_{ij})$ given by $Z_{kl}/Z_{ij}\mapsto(a_k/a_i)(c_l/c_j)=b_{kl}/b_{ij}$. That is exactly the ring map $\rho_{ij}$ defining $F$ on $D(b_{ij})$. The $D(b_{ij})$ cover $W$ (step 2), and these $W$ cover $P$, so $F=\sigma$ as morphisms on the relative-Proj spaces of the statement.

source.place: Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding), product sections and displayed chart map; Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), affine homogeneous-fraction characterization.; Tag 01NF (definition-projective-space): projective space over S as the base change of the one over Z, as in the 01WD proof's reduction to S=Spec(Z).

proof.text: For the free module of rank $(m+1)(n+1)$, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] identifies the target and its tautological twist with exactly the relative projective space and affine-local twist used here. The morphism it attaches to $(L,q)$ is the canonical relative-Proj morphism of the graded map $h^*\operatorname{Sym}\to\bigoplus_dL^{\otimes d}$ with degree-one part $q$; by [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] that graded map is the unique $\psi$ there and $F=r_{L,\psi}$, so $F$ is the morphism attached to $(L,q)$. Its quotient-compatible isomorphism gives $F^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$. Substitute $F=\sigma$ and $L=p_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes p_2^*\mathcal O(1)$. All applications allow arbitrary base schemes. If $S$ is empty the construction is on the empty scheme; if $m=0$ or $n=0$ the corresponding generating family has one member. Hence the same proof includes all stated boundary cases.

theorem nonempty_twistRestrict_segre_iso :
    Nonempty (twistRestrict (segre n m S) 1 ≅
      twistRestrict (pullback.fst (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) (ℙ(m; S) ↘ S)) 1 ⊗
        twistRestrict (pullback.snd (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) (ℙ(m; S) ↘ S)) 1)
lean.note: Existing upstream theorem, read in full at SegreTwist.lean:103-181. The base-change model and its twist express the same projective space and affine-local degree-one twisting module as the node, by the coordinate-preserving canonical Proj identification. No restriction on the base or nonemptiness hypothesis. No new Lean module.
